turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Doctor. I came in because, well, the thought of getting on an airplane right now just scares me so bad. I know it doesn't really make sense, but... my body just tells me that the plane is going to fall.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes an intense, disproportionate fear of flying on an airplane, recognizing that the fear does not rationally make sense.

turns.doctor_question: Does this intense fear only happen when you think about or are near airplanes, or do you also feel this kind of fear in other situations that have nothing to do with flying?
turns.patient_response: No, it's really just the airplanes. I don't have this problem with anything else. I drive to work, I take the elevator, I don't mind heights or being in small spaces... it's just flying. If I'm not thinking about getting on a plane, I'm completely fine.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient confirms that their intense fear is specifically isolated to airplanes and flying.
